frappe.name: get_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.get_doc(doctype: str | dict, name: str = None) -> Document
frappe.returnDescription: A complete Document controller instance containing all fields, child table records, and built-in methods.
frappe.docstring: Loads a full document from the database into memory. Use this when you want to read, edit, or execute business logic methods on a record.
frappe.example:
# 1. Load an existing document by its ID/Name:
employee = frappe.get_doc("Employee", "EMP-001")
print(employee.employee_name, employee.department)

# 2. Create a new document in memory from a dictionary:
new_todo = frappe.get_doc({
    "doctype": "ToDo",
    "description": "Review payroll report",
    "priority": "High"
})
new_todo.insert()

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: The DocType name as a string (e.g. 'Employee', 'Sales Invoice') OR a dictionary with document fields to initialize a new record.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The unique ID / Name of the document you want to load (e.g. 'EMP-001', 'ACC-SINV-2026-001'). Leave empty if passing a dictionary in the first argument.

frappe.name: get_cached_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.get_cached_doc(doctype: str, name: str = None) -> Document
frappe.returnDescription: Cached Document instance (fast memory lookup).
frappe.docstring: Loads a document from Redis memory cache if available, or fetches from the database. Use for read-only lookups on master data and settings DocTypes for maximum performance.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Name of the DocType to fetch from memory cache.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Document ID or name. For Single DocTypes (like 'System Settings'), you can omit this.

frappe.name: get_all
frappe.signature: frappe.get_all(doctype: str, filters: dict | list = None, fields: list[str] = None, order_by: str = None, limit_page_length: int = None) -> list[dict]
frappe.returnDescription: List of dictionaries matching your query filter. Each dictionary contains the requested fields.
frappe.docstring: Fetches a list of records from the database without checking user permissions (faster than get_list). Ideal for backend scripts, APIs, and background jobs.
frappe.example:
employees = frappe.get_all(
    "Employee",
    filters={"status": "Active", "department": "Sales"},
    fields=["name", "employee_name", "cell_number"],
    order_by="employee_name asc",
    limit_page_length=50
)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: The DocType name to query.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filtering conditions as key-value pairs or list of filter triplets.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: List of field names to retrieve.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sorting column and direction.

parameters.name: limit_page_length
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return.

frappe.name: get_list
frappe.signature: frappe.get_list(doctype: str, filters: dict = None, fields: list[str] = None, order_by: str = None, limit_page_length: int = 20) -> list[Document]
frappe.returnDescription: List of record dictionaries filtered by the active user's permissions.
frappe.docstring: Fetches a list of records while strictly enforcing the current user's role and permission rules. Use this for user-facing lists and portal views.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Target DocType name to query.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filter conditions dictionary or list of filter arrays.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: List of fieldnames to fetch (defaults to ["name"]).

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Sorting column order string.

parameters.name: limit_page_length
parameters.description: Number of records to retrieve per page.

frappe.name: new_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.new_doc(doctype: str) -> Document
frappe.returnDescription: Fresh, un-saved Document instance populated with default values.
frappe.docstring: Initializes a brand-new Document in memory with default values populated from the DocType schema.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Name of the DocType to create.

frappe.name: msgprint
frappe.signature: frappe.msgprint(msg: str, title: str = None, indicator: str = None, alert: bool = False)
frappe.returnDescription: None (Displays message modal/toast in Frappe Desk).
frappe.docstring: Displays a popup message dialog or notification toast to the user in the desk interface.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Message content or data structure to display.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Modal popup title heading.

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description: Color status indicator badge.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: If True, displays as floating toast message instead of modal.

frappe.name: throw
frappe.signature: frappe.throw(msg: str, exc: type[Exception] = frappe.ValidationError, title: str = None) -> None
frappe.returnDescription: Never returns (Raises ValidationError exception interrupting transaction).
frappe.docstring: Halts execution immediately, rolls back the current database transaction, and shows a red error dialog to the user.
frappe.example:
if not self.department:
    frappe.throw("Please select a Department before saving.", title="Missing Field")

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: Error message displayed to user.

parameters.name: exc
parameters.description: Exception class to raise (e.g. frappe.PermissionError, frappe.DoesNotExistError).

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Error modal heading title.

frappe.name: enqueue
frappe.signature: frappe.enqueue(method: str | callable, queue: str = 'default', timeout: int = 300, is_async: bool = True, now: bool = False, enqueue_after_commit: bool = False, **kwargs) -> str
frappe.returnDescription: Background RQ job object.
frappe.docstring: Runs a time-consuming Python function asynchronously in the background worker queue (Redis Queue) so it does not freeze the user interface.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Python dot-path string or callable function to execute in background worker.

parameters.name: queue
parameters.description: Redis worker queue priority tier.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum execution timeout in seconds before task fails.

parameters.name: is_async
parameters.description: Execute asynchronously via background worker (set False for synchronous testing).

parameters.name: now
parameters.description: Execute immediately in current thread instead of queuing.

parameters.name: enqueue_after_commit
parameters.description: Only push to Redis queue if current database transaction commits successfully.

parameters.name: kwargs
parameters.description: Keyword arguments passed directly to the target method.

frappe.name: sendmail
frappe.signature: frappe.sendmail(recipients: list[str] | str, sender: str = None, subject: str = None, message: str = None, as_markdown: bool = False, template: str = None, args: dict = None, delayed: bool = False, reference_doctype: str = None, reference_name: str = None, attachments: list[dict] = None) -> None
frappe.returnDescription: None (Queues or sends email message).
frappe.docstring: Queues and sends an email via the system Email Account. Links the email to a document timeline if reference_doctype is provided.
frappe.example:
frappe.sendmail(recipients=["user@example.com"], subject="Invoice Ready", message="

Your invoice is attached.

")

parameters.name: recipients
parameters.description: Recipient email addresses list or comma-separated string.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Sender email address (defaults to default outgoing email account).

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Email subject line.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Raw HTML or plain-text email body content.

parameters.name: as_markdown
parameters.description: Convert Markdown syntax in message body to HTML.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Jinja email template filename or DocType template name.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Context arguments dictionary supplied to Jinja email template.

parameters.name: delayed
parameters.description: Queue email in Email Queue for background sending rather than instant transmission.

parameters.name: reference_doctype
parameters.description: Reference DocType to link email communication history with.

parameters.name: reference_name
parameters.description: Reference document name / ID.

parameters.name: attachments
parameters.description: List of attachment dictionaries with fname and fcontent.

frappe.name: publish_realtime
frappe.signature: frappe.publish_realtime(event: str, message: dict | str = None, room: str = None, user: str = None, doctype: str = None, docname: str = None, after_commit: bool = False) -> None
frappe.returnDescription: None (Transmits WebSocket packet to connected browser clients).
frappe.docstring: Pushes a real-time WebSocket event message from the server to connected browser clients instantly via SocketIO.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: WebSocket event identifier string.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Payload dictionary or string transmitted to client listener.

parameters.name: room
parameters.description: Broadcast room target.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Specific recipient user email; if omitted, broadcasts to all connected users or room.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType context filter.

parameters.name: docname
parameters.description: Document name context filter.

parameters.name: after_commit
parameters.description: Emit event only after active SQL transaction commits.

frappe.name: log_error
frappe.signature: frappe.log_error(title: str = None, message: str = None, reference_doctype: str = None, reference_name: str = None) -> Document
frappe.returnDescription: The created `Error Log` Document containing the recorded traceback, error title, and optional reference linkage.
frappe.docstring: Writes a detailed error and traceback to the `Error Log` DocType in the database. Essential for background jobs, webhooks, and asynchronous tasks where errors must be preserved and investigated in Frappe Desk without breaking execution.
frappe.example:
# 1. Log an exception in a try/except block with custom title:
try:
    process_order(order_id)
except Exception as e:
    frappe.log_error(title=f"Order Processing Failed: {order_id}", message=frappe.get_traceback())

# 2. Attach error log to a reference document (Frappe v14+):
frappe.log_error(
    title="Payment Gateway Timeout",
    message=response.text,
    reference_doctype="Sales Invoice",
    reference_name="ACC-SINV-2026-0001"
)

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A short, descriptive heading for the error shown in the Error Log list view.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The full error message, JSON payload, or Python traceback string (`frappe.get_traceback()`). If omitted inside an except block in v15+, Frappe captures the traceback automatically.

parameters.name: reference_doctype
parameters.description: DocType associated with the error (enables direct linking from Error Log to the record).

parameters.name: reference_name
parameters.description: Name / ID of the specific document where the error originated.

frappe.name: logger

frappe.example:

log.info("Syncing employees with external HR API...")

frappe.signature: frappe.respond_as_web_page(title: str, html: str, success: bool = None, http_status_code: int = None) -> None
frappe.docstring: Renders custom HTML response as full website page for web requests.

Your payment was successful

', success=True)

parameters.name: html

parameters.name: success

frappe.name: whitelist
frappe.signature: frappe.whitelist(allow_guest: bool = False, xss_safe: bool = False, methods: list[str] = None)
frappe.returnDescription: Decorates a Python function to make it callable via HTTP API / frappe.call.
frappe.docstring: Decorator that exposes a server-side Python function to the client-side JavaScript (`frappe.call`), Mobile Apps, REST API (`/api/method/app.path.func`), and Webhooks. By default, only authenticated users can invoke whitelisted methods.

parameters.name: allow_guest
parameters.description: Set to True if guests / unauthenticated public visitors should be allowed to execute this API.

parameters.name: methods
parameters.description: Restrict allowed HTTP request methods (e.g. ["POST", "PUT"]). Defaults to all methods.

parameters.name: xss_safe
parameters.description: Mark output as safe HTML to prevent automatic escaping.

frappe.name: copy_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.copy_doc(doc: Document | dict, ignore_no_copy: bool = True) -> Document
frappe.returnDescription: A new cloned Document instance in memory (not yet inserted into database).
frappe.docstring: Creates a deep copy of a document and all of its child table records in memory. Automatically clears the primary key (`name`), creation dates, modified timestamps, and submission status (`docstatus=0`), allowing you to modify and `.insert()` as a new record.
frappe.example:
# Duplicate an existing Sales Order for a new customer:
original_so = frappe.get_doc("Sales Order", "SO-2026-0001")
new_so = frappe.copy_doc(original_so)
new_so.customer = "New Customer Inc"
new_so.transaction_date = frappe.utils.today()
new_so.insert()

parameters.name: doc
parameters.description: The source document instance to duplicate.

parameters.name: ignore_no_copy
parameters.description: If True, fields marked with "No Copy" in DocType schema are skipped and not cloned.

frappe.name: rename_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.rename_doc(doctype: str, old: str, new: str, force: bool = False, merge: bool = False, ignore_permissions: bool = False) -> str
frappe.returnDescription: The new document name/ID.
frappe.docstring: Renames a document primary key (`name`) and automatically updates all foreign key references, Link fields, and child tables across the entire database. If `merge=True`, merges all references from `old` into `new` and deletes `old`.
frappe.example:
# 1. Rename a customer code safely across all invoices and orders:
frappe.rename_doc("Customer", "CUST-OLD-01", "CUST-ACME-01")

# 2. Merge duplicate items into one master item:
frappe.rename_doc("Item", "WIDGET-OLD", "WIDGET-MASTER", merge=True)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: The DocType name of the record being renamed.

parameters.name: old
parameters.description: The current primary key / name of the document.

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: The new primary key / name to assign.

parameters.name: merge
parameters.description: If True, merges the old record into an existing target record and deletes the old one.

frappe.name: delete_doc
frappe.signature: frappe.delete_doc(doctype: str, name: str, force: bool = False, ignore_permissions: bool = False, delete_permanently: bool = False)
frappe.returnDescription: None
frappe.docstring: Deletes a document from the database along with its child table rows, attachments, activity feeds, and dynamic links. By default, moves deleted documents to the "Deleted Document" trash table unless `delete_permanently=True`.
frappe.example:
# 1. Safely delete a draft Quotation:
frappe.delete_doc("Quotation", "QTN-2026-0004")

# 2. Force delete permanently in a cleanup script:
frappe.delete_doc("Log Entry", "LOG-00123", force=True, delete_permanently=True)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType name of the document to delete.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Primary key / name of the document.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: If True, bypasses checks for linked records and submitted status.

parameters.name: delete_permanently
parameters.description: If True, bypasses trash and deletes row permanently from database.

frappe.name: get_meta
frappe.signature: frappe.get_meta(doctype: str, cached: bool = True) -> Meta
frappe.returnDescription: DocType Meta schema instance containing field definitions, properties, and permissions.
frappe.docstring: Fetches the DocType metadata definition (`Meta` object). Allows you to programmatically inspect fields, check if a field exists, get field types, link targets, and read permission rules.
frappe.example:
# Inspect DocType schema:
meta = frappe.get_meta("Customer")
print(meta.has_field("tax_id"))  # True/False

# Loop through all currency fields:
for field in meta.get_currency_fields():
    print(field.fieldname, field.label)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Name of the DocType to inspect.

frappe.name: get_cached_value
frappe.signature: frappe.get_cached_value(doctype: str, name: str, fieldname: str | list[str] | tuple, as_dict: bool = False) -> Any
frappe.returnDescription: Field value or dict/tuple of field values fetched from Redis cache.
frappe.docstring: Ultra-fast memory-cached database lookup for single or multiple fields. If the value exists in Redis memory cache, it returns immediately without executing a SQL query. Ideal for high-traffic lookups on master records like Company, Settings, or Currency.
frappe.example:
# 1. Fetch a single field from memory cache:
currency = frappe.get_cached_value("Company", "Acme Corp", "default_currency")

# 2. Fetch multiple fields as a dictionary:
company_info = frappe.get_cached_value(
    "Company",
    "Acme Corp",
    ["default_currency", "country", "tax_id"],
    as_dict=True
)
print(company_info.default_currency, company_info.country)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Document ID / Name.

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: Field name or list of field names to retrieve.

frappe.name: get_roles
frappe.signature: frappe.get_roles(username: str = None) -> list[str]
frappe.returnDescription: List of role names assigned to the user.
frappe.docstring: Returns a list of all role names assigned to a given user. If username is omitted, returns the roles for the currently logged-in session user (`frappe.session.user`).
frappe.example:
# Check if the current user is an Accounts Manager or System Manager:
roles = frappe.get_roles()
if "Accounts Manager" in roles or "System Manager" in roles:
    print("User is authorized for financial approval")

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Email / user ID to check roles for. Defaults to active session user.

frappe.name: has_permission
frappe.signature: frappe.has_permission(doctype: str, ptype: str = "read", doc: Document | str = None, user: str = None) -> bool
frappe.returnDescription: True if user has permission; False otherwise.
frappe.docstring: Checks if the user has the specified permission ("read", "write", "create", "submit", "cancel", "delete", "print", "email") on a DocType or a specific document instance (evaluating user permissions and role permissions).
frappe.example:
# Check if current user can edit a specific Sales Order:
can_edit = frappe.has_permission("Sales Order", ptype="write", doc="SO-2026-0001")
if not can_edit:
    frappe.throw("You do not have permission to modify this Sales Order.", frappe.PermissionError)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType name to verify permission on.

parameters.name: ptype
parameters.description: The permission level to check.

parameters.name: doc
parameters.description: Optional Document instance or document name to evaluate document-level User Permissions.

frappe.db.name: get_value
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.get_value(doctype: str, filters: str | dict | list, fieldname: str | list[str] = 'name', as_dict: bool = False) -> Any | dict | None
frappe.db.returnDescription: The single field value, a tuple of values, a dictionary (if as_dict=True), or None if no record matches.
frappe.db.docstring: Reads specific field values directly from the database table with a fast SQL query without loading the full Document into memory. Highly recommended for quick field lookups.
frappe.db.example: status = frappe.db.get_value("Employee", "EMP-001", "status")

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: The DocType database table to query.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Document ID string OR filter conditions dictionary.

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: The field name or list of field names you want to retrieve.

parameters.name: as_dict
parameters.description: Set True to return the result as a dictionary.

frappe.db.name: get_values
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.get_values(doctype: str, filters: dict | list | str = None, fieldname: str | list[str] = "*", as_dict: bool = False, order_by: str = None) -> list
frappe.db.returnDescription: List of matching records formatted as dicts (if as_dict=True) or tuples of column values.
frappe.db.docstring: Fetches multiple records and multiple columns directly from the database without loading full Document instances into memory. Much faster than `frappe.get_all` when you only need raw column values.
frappe.db.example:
# 1. Fetch specific columns as a list of dictionaries:
customers = frappe.db.get_values(
    "Customer",
    filters={"customer_group": "Commercial", "disabled": 0},
    fieldname=["name", "customer_name", "territory", "credit_limit"],
    as_dict=True
)
for c in customers:
    print(c.customer_name, c.credit_limit)

# 2. Fetch single column values as flat list:
active_emails = [r[0] for r in frappe.db.get_values("User", {"enabled": 1}, "email")]

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType table name to query.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filter conditions to match rows.

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: List of fieldnames to retrieve from the database table.

parameters.name: as_dict
parameters.description: If True, returns records as dictionaries with field names as keys.

frappe.db.name: set_value
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.set_value(doctype: str, name: str | dict, fieldname: str | dict, value: any = None, update_modified: bool = True) -> None
frappe.db.returnDescription: None. Updates database record directly.
frappe.db.docstring: Directly updates a field or fields in the database table with a fast SQL UPDATE statement without triggering document validation hooks.
frappe.db.example: frappe.db.set_value("Employee", "EMP-001", "status", "Left")

parameters.name: doctype

parameters.name: name

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: Fieldname to update or dictionary of multiple key-value pairs.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: New value to assign (omit if fieldname is a dictionary).

parameters.name: update_modified
parameters.description: Update modified timestamp and modified_by user columns.

frappe.db.name: get_single_value
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.get_single_value(doctype: str, fieldname: str, cache: bool = True) -> Any
frappe.db.returnDescription: The value of the requested field in the Single DocType.
frappe.db.docstring: Fetches a single setting or field value from a Single DocType (e.g. `System Settings`, `Stock Settings`, `HR Settings`). Single DocTypes store all their field settings as key-value pairs in the `tabSingles` table.
frappe.db.example:
# 1. Get default company from Global Defaults:
default_company = frappe.db.get_single_value("Global Defaults", "default_company")

# 2. Check if 2FA is enforced in System Settings:
two_factor_enabled = frappe.db.get_single_value("System Settings", "enable_two_factor_auth")

frappe.db.name: set_single_value
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.set_single_value(doctype: str, fieldname: str, value: Any)
frappe.db.returnDescription: None
frappe.db.docstring: Updates a single setting/field value in a Single DocType (stored in `tabSingles`) directly in the database without instantiating the full document.
frappe.db.example:
# Update system maintenance mode or backup settings programmatically:
frappe.db.set_single_value("System Settings", "allow_error_traceback", 0)
frappe.db.set_single_value("Global Defaults", "default_currency", "USD")

parameters.name: fieldname

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: New value to store.

frappe.db.name: exists
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.exists(doctype: str | dict, name: str | dict = None) -> str | None
frappe.db.returnDescription: Returns the document name/ID if the record exists, or None if it does not exist.
frappe.db.docstring: Checks whether a record exists in the database table. Very fast boolean check.
frappe.db.example:
if frappe.db.exists("Customer", "Acme Corp"):

frappe.db.name: count
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.count(doctype: str, filters: dict | list = None, distinct: bool = False) -> int
frappe.db.returnDescription: Total number of rows matching the query.
frappe.db.docstring: Executes a high-speed `SELECT COUNT(*)` query in SQL to count records matching your filters. Always use `frappe.db.count()` instead of `len(frappe.get_all())` because it does not load records into Python memory.
frappe.db.example:
# 1. Count active employees in Sales:
sales_count = frappe.db.count("Employee", {"department": "Sales", "status": "Active"})

# 2. Count overdue invoices:
overdue_count = frappe.db.count("Sales Invoice", filters=[
    ["outstanding_amount", ">", 0],
    ["due_date", "<", frappe.utils.today()]
])

parameters.name: filters

frappe.db.returnDescription: None.

parameters.description: DocType table name.

parameters.description: Document ID or filter condition dictionary.

frappe.db.name: commit
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.commit()
frappe.db.returnDescription: None.
frappe.db.docstring: Explicitly commits the current database transaction. Note: Frappe commits automatically at the end of each web request.
frappe.db.example: frappe.db.commit()

frappe.db.name: rollback
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.rollback()
frappe.db.returnDescription: None.
frappe.db.docstring: Rolls back all uncommitted database changes in the current request.
frappe.db.example: frappe.db.rollback()

frappe.db.name: sql
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.sql(query: str, values: dict | tuple = None, as_dict: bool = False) -> list[dict] | list[tuple]
frappe.db.returnDescription: List of query result rows as dictionaries or tuples.
frappe.db.docstring: Executes a raw SQL query against the database. Always use parameterized %(val)s queries to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities.
frappe.db.example:
results = frappe.db.sql("""
    SELECT name, employee_name
    FROM `tabEmployee`
    WHERE status = %(status)s
""", {"status": "Active"}, as_dict=True)

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: SQL query string with %(param)s placeholders.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Dictionary or tuple of values to safely bind.

parameters.name: as_dict
parameters.description: Set True to return rows as dictionaries.

frappe.db.name: savepoint
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.savepoint(save_point_name: str)
frappe.db.docstring: Creates a named database transaction savepoint. Allows you to partially roll back nested operations inside a `try...except` block without discarding the outer database transaction.
frappe.db.example:
savepoint_id = "process_order_batch"
frappe.db.savepoint(savepoint_id)

try:
    # Attempt critical nested operation:
    process_third_party_payment(doc)
    frappe.db.release_savepoint(savepoint_id)
except Exception as e:
    # Roll back only the payment attempt, keeping previous order changes:
    frappe.db.rollback(save_point=savepoint_id)
    doc.db_set("payment_error", str(e))

parameters.name: save_point_name
parameters.description: Unique identifier string for this savepoint.

frappe.db.returnDescription: Sets a transaction savepoint.

frappe.db.name: release_savepoint
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.release_savepoint(save_point_name: str)
frappe.db.docstring: Releases an active savepoint without rolling back.
frappe.db.example: frappe.db.release_savepoint('my_savepoint')

parameters.name: save_point_name
parameters.description: Savepoint name

frappe.db.returnDescription: None (Releases active savepoint).

frappe.db.name: table_exists
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.table_exists(doctype: str) -> bool
frappe.db.docstring: Checks whether database table exists for given DocType.

if frappe.db.table_exists('Employee'):

if frappe.db.has_column('Employee', 'cell_number'):

frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.multisql(query_dict: dict, values: dict | tuple = None, as_dict: bool = True) -> list

frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.add_index(doctype: str, fields: list[str], index_name: str = None) -> None
frappe.db.docstring: Creates database index on DocType table columns for query optimization.
frappe.db.example: frappe.db.add_index('Sales Invoice', ['customer', 'posting_date'])

parameters.name: doctype

parameters.description: Custom index identifier name in database schema.

frappe.db.returnDescription: None (Creates database index).

frappe.db.name: get_descendants
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.get_descendants(doctype: str, name: str) -> list[str]
frappe.db.returnDescription: List of primary key names of all child nodes in tree hierarchy.
frappe.db.docstring: Returns all descendant child records for a given node in a NestedSet / Tree DocType (e.g. Chart of Accounts, Territory, Item Group, Department). Uses fast left/right nested set index indexing (`lft` and `rgt`).
frappe.db.example:
# Fetch all child accounts under "Current Assets":
child_accounts = frappe.db.get_descendants("Account", "Current Assets - ACME")
# Query all transactions belonging to any child account:
balances = frappe.get_all("GL Entry", filters={"account": ["in", child_accounts]})

frappe.db.name: bulk_insert
frappe.db.signature: frappe.db.bulk_insert(doctype: str, fields: list[str], values: list[list | tuple], ignore_duplicates: bool = False)
frappe.db.returnDescription: Inserts batch rows directly into MySQL/PostgreSQL table.
frappe.db.docstring: Executes a high-performance batch SQL multi-row insert directly into the DocType table. It bypasses document controller hooks and validations, making it up to 100x faster for importing thousands of records or streaming sensor/log data.
frappe.db.example:
# Batch insert 500 log rows in a single SQL query:
fields = ["name", "timestamp", "log_level", "message"]
values = [
    [frappe.generate_hash(length=10), frappe.utils.now_datetime(), "INFO", f"Task {i} finished"]
    for i in range(500)
]
frappe.db.bulk_insert("Activity Log", fields, values, ignore_duplicates=True)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Target DocType table.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Column names to insert.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Matrix of row values to insert.

Document.name: validate
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Called on every save before changes are written to the database. Use this to perform business validations and throw errors if rules are violated.

Document.name: before_save
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Executed right after validate(), right before writing updates to the database table.
Document.example:
def before_save(self):
    self.total_amount = sum(item.amount for item in self.items)

Document.name: on_update
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Triggered immediately after the document has been written and saved in the database.
Document.example:
def on_update(self):
    self.notify_parent_project()

Document.name: before_insert
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Runs only once when a brand-new document is first being inserted into the database.
Document.example:
def before_insert(self):
    self.initial_status = "Draft"

Document.name: after_insert
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Runs immediately after a brand-new document has been created in the database.
Document.example:
def after_insert(self):
    frappe.sendmail(recipients=self.owner, subject="Welcome!")

Document.name: on_submit
Document.returnDescription: Controller hook called when document is submitted (docstatus becomes 1).
Document.docstring: Lifecycle controller hook executed immediately when a submittable document (`is_submittable = 1`) is submitted by the user. Use this to create General Ledger entries, deduct stock balances, update linked documents, or send official notifications.
Document.example:
class SalesInvoice(Document):
    def on_submit(self):
        # 1. Post accounting ledger entries:
        self.make_gl_entries()
        # 2. Deduct inventory from warehouse:
        self.update_stock_ledger()
        # 3. Notify customer:
        frappe.sendmail(
            recipients=[self.contact_email],
            subject=f"Invoice {self.name} Confirmed",
            message="Thank you! Your payment invoice is attached."
        )

Document.name: on_cancel
Document.returnDescription: Controller hook called when document is cancelled (docstatus becomes 2).
Document.docstring: Lifecycle controller hook executed when a submitted document is cancelled by the user. Use this to reverse accounting GL entries, return reserved stock back to the warehouse, and unlink dependent transactions.
Document.example:
class SalesInvoice(Document):
    def on_cancel(self):
        # 1. Reverse accounting transactions:
        self.make_gl_entries(cancel=True)
        # 2. Return deducted stock back to inventory:
        self.update_stock_ledger(cancel=True)
        frappe.msgprint(f"Invoice {self.name} cancelled and ledger entries reversed.")

Document.name: on_trash
Document.docstring: Lifecycle Hook: Triggered right before a document is permanently deleted from the database.
Document.example:
def on_trash(self):
    self.clean_up_attachments()

Document.name: insert
Document.signature: doc.insert(ignore_permissions: bool = False, ignore_links: bool = False) -> Document
Document.docstring: Inserts this new document into the database table, runs before_insert / validate hooks, and generates its permanent naming ID.
Document.example:
doc = frappe.new_doc("Customer")
doc.customer_name = "Acme"
doc.insert()

parameters.name: ignore_permissions
parameters.description: Bypass permission validation check during insert.

parameters.name: ignore_links
parameters.description: Bypass dynamic Link and Foreign Key validation checks.

Document.name: save
Document.docstring: Saves changes made to an existing document, runs validation hooks, and updates the database row.
Document.example:
doc.department = "Human Resources"
doc.save()

parameters.name: ignore_permissions
parameters.description: If True, ignores role permission checks.

Document.name: submit
Document.docstring: Submits a submittable document (changes docstatus from 0 to 1) and triggers on_submit hooks.
Document.example: doc.submit()

Document.name: cancel
Document.docstring: Cancels a submitted document (changes docstatus from 1 to 2) and triggers on_cancel hooks.
Document.example: doc.cancel()

Document.name: append
Document.signature: doc.append(table_fieldname: str, value: dict = None) -> Document
Document.returnDescription: The newly created child table row object.
Document.docstring: Appends a brand new row to a child table. It automatically assigns the correct row index (`idx`), links the parent record, and initializes default values. You can pass a dictionary of field values directly or modify the returned child row object.
Document.example:
# Method 1: Append with a dictionary of values
doc.append("items", {
    "item_code": "ITEM-001",
    "qty": 5,
    "rate": 120.00
})

# Method 2: Append and modify the returned row object directly
new_row = doc.append("items")
new_row.item_code = "ITEM-002"
new_row.qty = 10
new_row.rate = 50.00

parameters.name: table_fieldname
parameters.description: Fieldname of the Table / Child Table in the parent DocType.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Dictionary of field values to set on the new child row.

Document.name: db_set
Document.signature: doc.db_set(fieldname: str | dict, value: Any = None, update_modified: bool = True, notify: bool = False)
Document.docstring: Directly and instantly updates specific fields in the database for this document. Unlike `doc.save()`, `db_set` does NOT trigger lifecycle hooks (`validate`, `before_save`, `on_update`), making it very fast for updating statuses, flags, or background task outcomes without triggering full document validation rules.
Document.example:
# 1. Update a single field instantly:
doc.db_set("workflow_state", "Approved")

# 2. Update multiple fields at once without updating modified timestamp:
doc.db_set({
    "last_sync_datetime": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
    "sync_status": "Completed"
}, update_modified=False)

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: Field name as string, OR a dictionary mapping multiple field names to their new values.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to assign (when passing a string in the first argument).

parameters.name: update_modified
parameters.description: If True, updates the `modified` and `modified_by` audit fields of the document.

Document.name: as_dict
Document.signature: doc.as_dict(no_nulls: bool = False, no_default_fields: bool = False, convert_dates_to_str: bool = False) -> dict
Document.returnDescription: Python dictionary containing all document fields and child tables.
Document.docstring: Converts the entire Document controller instance and its child tables into a standard, clean Python dictionary. Ideal for returning data in REST API responses, serializing to JSON, or passing into templates.
Document.example:
# 1. Convert document to dictionary for API response:
employee_doc = frappe.get_doc("Employee", "EMP-001")
data = employee_doc.as_dict(no_nulls=True)

# 2. Clean dict without internal default fields (creation, modified, etc.):
clean_data = employee_doc.as_dict(no_default_fields=True)

parameters.name: no_nulls
parameters.description: If True, strips keys with None / null values from the resulting dictionary.

parameters.name: no_default_fields
parameters.description: If True, omits standard metadata fields like `name`, `owner`, `creation`, `modified`.

Document.name: is_new
Document.returnDescription: True if document has never been saved into the database; False otherwise.
Document.docstring: Checks whether the document is an in-memory new record that has not yet been committed to the database. Internally checks `doc.__islocal` and `doc.get("__islocal")`.

Document.name: get_url
Document.returnDescription: Direct desk URL string to open the document.
Document.docstring: Returns the complete browser URL path pointing to this document in desk.
Document.example: url = doc.get_url()

Document.name: add_comment
Document.signature: doc.add_comment(comment_type: str = "Comment", text: str = None, comment_by: str = None) -> Document
Document.docstring: Adds an activity timeline note, mention, or system comment to this document. Comments appear in the sidebar/timeline of the document in Frappe Desk.
Document.example:
# 1. Add a user discussion comment:
doc = frappe.get_doc("Lead", "LEAD-2026-0001")
doc.add_comment("Comment", text="Spoke with client. They requested a quote for 50 units.")

# 2. Add an automated system workflow note:
doc.add_comment("Workflow", text="Document auto-approved based on Credit Rating A+")

parameters.name: comment_type
parameters.description: Type of timeline comment to create.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The comment text or markdown message to display on the timeline.

Document.name: add_tag
Document.docstring: Attaches a color-coded tag to this document for filtering, categorization, and Kanban grouping in Frappe Desk. If the tag does not exist globally, Frappe automatically creates it in `__global_tags`.
Document.example:
doc = frappe.get_doc("Lead", "LEAD-00012")
doc.add_tag("High Priority")
doc.add_tag("Q4-Deal")

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Tag name

Document.name: run_method
Document.docstring: Dynamically invokes a method defined on the DocType controller class or Server Scripts. Also triggers document event hooks configured in `hooks.py` (doc_events). Useful when you need to execute business logic dynamically by method name.
Document.example:
# 1. Dynamically run a method on an invoice:
doc.run_method("calculate_taxes_and_totals")

# 2. Run a custom processing method with parameters:
result = doc.run_method("generate_qr_code", format="PNG", size=256)

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Name of the method to execute on the Document instance.

Document.returnDescription: The return value of the executed controller method or Server Script hook.

Document.name: queue_action
Document.docstring: Enqueues standard document submission (`submit`) or cancellation (`cancel`) actions into the background Redis worker queue. Use this for heavy documents (e.g. Invoices with hundreds of child rows or complex stock ledgers) to prevent HTTP request timeouts in the browser.
Document.example:
# Queue a heavy invoice for background submission:
invoice = frappe.get_doc("Sales Invoice", "ACC-SINV-2026-00042")
invoice.queue_action("submit", timeout=600)
frappe.msgprint("Invoice submitted in the background. You will be notified once complete.")

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action to execute asynchronously in the background queue.

Document.name: has_value_changed
Document.docstring: Checks if a field's value has changed during the current save cycle by comparing against `get_doc_before_save()`. Returns True if modified, False otherwise.

parameters.name: fieldname
parameters.description: Fieldname to check

Document.returnDescription: True if field value changed in memory vs database.

Document.name: get_doc_before_save
Document.returnDescription: Previous snapshot of the document prior to current changes, or None for newly created records.
Document.docstring: Returns the previous in-memory state of the document as it was before the user made edits. Essential for detecting changed fields, auditing modifications, and calculating balance differentials in `validate()` or `before_save()`.

frappe.utils.name: money_in_words
frappe.utils.signature: frappe.utils.money_in_words(number: float | int, main_currency: str = None, fraction_currency: str = None) -> str
frappe.utils.returnDescription: Capitalized string representation of monetary amount in words.
frappe.utils.docstring: Converts a numeric monetary amount into full written English words formatted for financial checks, official receipts, and invoices (e.g. "USD One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty and Fifty Cents Only").
frappe.utils.example:

frappe.model.naming.name: getseries
frappe.model.naming.signature: frappe.model.naming.getseries(key: str, digits: int = None, doctype: str = None, step: int = 1) -> str
frappe.model.naming.returnDescription: The next formatted sequential number as a string (padded with leading zeros if digits is provided).
frappe.model.naming.docstring: Atomically increments and returns the next sequential number for a given naming series prefix from the database table `tabSeries`. Because it updates the database counter atomically with row-level locks, it is 100% safe from race conditions and duplicate IDs when multiple users or background jobs generate documents simultaneously.
frappe.model.naming.example:
# 1. Basic usage - fetch the next 5-digit number (e.g. '00001', '00002'):
from frappe.model.naming import getseries

next_seq = getseries("INV-2026-", 5)
full_invoice_id = f"INV-2026-{next_seq}"
# Result: "INV-2026-00001"

# 2. Inside a DocType custom autoname() controller method:
from frappe.model.naming import getseries
from frappe.model.document import Document

class SalesContract(Document):
    def autoname(self):
        year = frappe.utils.nowdate()[:4]
        prefix = f"CNT-{self.company_abbr}-{year}-"
        # Generate next 4-digit sequence: "0001", "0002", etc.
        self.name = f"{prefix}{getseries(prefix, 4)}"

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The prefix pattern identifying the sequence counter in `tabSeries` table (e.g. "ACC-SINV-", "EMP-2026-").

parameters.name: digits
parameters.description: Number of digits to pad with leading zeros. E.g. digits=5 formats 1 as "00001". If None, returns raw string representation of the integer.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Optional DocType name linked to this naming series.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Amount to increment the counter by (default is 1).

frappe.model.naming.name: make_autoname
frappe.model.naming.signature: frappe.model.naming.make_autoname(key: str, doctype: str = None, doc: Document = None) -> str
frappe.model.naming.returnDescription: Unique generated naming ID formatted according to the series pattern.
frappe.model.naming.docstring: Generates a unique document ID based on a standard Frappe series pattern (e.g. `ACC-SINV-.YYYY.-.#####` or `.FY.`). It automatically evaluates year (.YYYY.), month (.MM.), date (.DD.), fiscal year (.FY.), and digit padding (.#####).
frappe.model.naming.example:
# 1. Dynamic series with year and 5-digit counter:
new_id = frappe.model.naming.make_autoname("SAL-SLIP-.YYYY.-.#####", "Salary Slip")
# Result: "SAL-SLIP-2026-00001"

# 2. In custom autoname() with field substitution:
class CustomOrder(Document):
    def autoname(self):
        # Format: ORD-CUSTNAME-00001
        self.name = frappe.model.naming.make_autoname(f"ORD-{self.customer_code}-.#####", self.doctype, self)

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Naming series format string containing tags like .YYYY., .MM., .DD., .FY., and .##### for numbers.

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: Reference DocType name for tracking the series.

parameters.name: doc
parameters.description: Document instance used for dynamic field replacements in naming format strings.

frappe.model.naming.name: revert_series_if_last
frappe.model.naming.signature: frappe.model.naming.revert_series_if_last(key: str, name: str, doc: Document = None) -> None
frappe.model.naming.returnDescription: Does not return a value; decrements counter in database if applicable.
frappe.model.naming.docstring: Rolls back / decrements the sequential counter in `tabSeries` if the document being cancelled or deleted was the most recent (last) document created in that series. This prevents gaps in numbering sequences when the latest created document is immediately deleted.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The series prefix key in `tabSeries` to check and potentially decrement.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The document name being deleted or cancelled.

parameters.name: doc
parameters.description: The document instance being discarded.

frappe.model.naming.signature: frappe.model.naming.parse_naming_series(parts: list[str] | str, doc: Document = None, pattern: str = None) -> str
frappe.model.naming.returnDescription: Parsed naming prefix string with date and field values evaluated.
frappe.model.naming.docstring: Evaluates dynamic tokens in a naming series format string such as `.YYYY.` (4-digit year), `.YY.` (2-digit year), `.MM.` (2-digit month), `.DD.` (day of month), `.FY.` (fiscal year), and `{field_name}` (field values from document).

frappe.qb.name: DocType
frappe.qb.returnDescription: QueryBuilder table object with typed field references.
frappe.qb.docstring: Creates a QueryBuilder table representation for a DocType. Used to construct type-safe SQL queries with JOINs, nested WHERE criteria, GROUP BY, and aggregations without raw SQL string concatenation.
frappe.qb.example:
# Build a type-safe SQL query with JOIN and WHERE filter:
inv = frappe.qb.DocType("Sales Invoice")
cust = frappe.qb.DocType("Customer")

query = (
    frappe.qb.from_(inv)
    .inner_join(cust)
    .on(inv.customer == cust.name)
    .select(inv.name, inv.grand_total, cust.customer_name, cust.territory)
    .where(inv.docstatus == 1)
    .where(inv.grand_total > 5000)
    .orderby(inv.grand_total, order=frappe.qb.desc)
)
results = query.run(as_dict=True)

parameters.name: doctype
parameters.description: DocType name to build table schema for.

frappe.qb.name: from_
frappe.qb.docstring: Initiates a QueryBuilder `SELECT` query starting from the specified DocType table.
frappe.qb.example:
# Query active users with count of assigned tasks:
user = frappe.qb.DocType("User")
todo = frappe.qb.DocType("ToDo")

query = (
    frappe.qb.from_(user)
    .left_join(todo).on(user.name == todo.allocated_to)
    .select(user.name, user.full_name, frappe.query_builder.functions.Count(todo.name).as_("task_count"))
    .where(user.enabled == 1)
    .groupby(user.name)
)
data = query.run(as_dict=True)

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Target table or DocType instance to select from.

frappe.qb.returnDescription: Raw table reference for database tables that are not standard DocTypes.
frappe.qb.docstring: Creates a QueryBuilder table reference for non-DocType tables (e.g. `tabSeries`, `tabSessions`, or custom system tables).

parameters.name: table_name
parameters.description: Raw SQL database table name.
